<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:A}
For every $d\ge1$,
\[
p(d)=2^{-d}\sum_{w\in\{T,\,T+1\}^{d}} 2^{-\omega_0(K(w))} .
\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:bl} each $f$ with $m(f)>0$ contributes $m(f)\,2^{-\omega_0(f)}=1$ to
$\sum_f m(f)2^{-\omega_0(f)}$ and each $f$ with $m(f)=0$ contributes $0$; the left-hand
sum is therefore the number of $f$ with $m(f)>0$. Expanding $m(f)$ by the
word parametrisation underlying \eqref{eq:sum} turns it into the stated sum over words.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:B}
Let $f$ be monic with $\gcd(f,T(T+1))=1$. Then
\[
\sum_{P\mid f}\psi_P(f)=0 .
\]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:C}
Let $P$ be a monic irreducible of degree $j\ge2$ and put $Q=|P|=2^{j}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Let $n\ge j$. As $h$ runs over the monic polynomials of degree $n$ with
$P\nmid h$, one has $\psi_P(Ph)=0$ for exactly $2^{\,n-j}\bigl(2^{\,j-1}-1\bigr)$
values of $h$, that is for a proportion exactly $\dfrac{Q-2}{2(Q-1)}$.
\item[(ii)] Let $e\ge2$ and $n\ge ej$. As $h$ runs over the monic polynomials of
degree $n$ with $P\nmid h$, one has $\psi_P(P^{e}h)=0$ for exactly half of the values
of $h$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{conj}
For every real $x>0$, as $d\to\infty$,
\[
\sum_{\substack{f\ \mathrm{monic}\\ \deg f=d}} m(f)\,x^{\omega_0(f)}
\ \sim\ 2^{d}\,H(x)\,\frac{d^{\,x-1}}{\Gamma(x)},
\qquad
H(x)=\frac{9}{2}\,4^{-x}\prod_{\deg P\ge2}
\Bigl(1+\frac{x}{|P|}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\frac{1}{|P|}\Bigr)^{x},
\]
the product being over the monic irreducibles of $\mathbb{A}$ of degree at least two.
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:H1}
$H(1)=1$, so that Conjecture \ref{conj} at $x=1$ reduces to \eqref{eq:sum}.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
$H(1)=\tfrac98\prod_{\deg P\ge2}(1-|P|^{-2})$. The zeta function of $\mathbb{A}$ gives
$\prod_{P}(1-|P|^{-2})^{-1}=\zeta_\mathbb{A}(2)=\sum_{d\ge0}2^{d}4^{-d}=2$, so
$\prod_{P}(1-|P|^{-2})=\tfrac12$; removing the two places of degree one divides this by
$(1-\tfrac14)^2=\tfrac9{16}$, leaving $\tfrac89$. Hence $H(1)=\tfrac98\cdot\tfrac89=1$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor}
Granting Conjecture \ref{conj},
\[
p(d)\ \sim\ L\,d^{-1/2},\qquad
L=\frac{9}{4\sqrt\pi}\prod_{\deg P\ge2}\Bigl(1+\frac{1}{2|P|}\Bigr)
\Bigl(1-\frac{1}{|P|}\Bigr)^{1/2}=1.2116120743\ldots
\]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
For $f=P^{e}$ with $P$ a non-linear irreducible, Theorem \ref{thm:B} forces
$\psi_P(f)=0$. Together with the criterion verified in Section \ref{sec:num}, this
recovers in one line the theorem of Mesirov and Sweet \cite{MS} that
$m(P)=2$ for every non-linear irreducible $P$, and its extension to prime powers
\cite[Prop.~3.17]{LaTh}, both as reported in \cite[\S4.2.2]{Ma}.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
